Acknowledgement of Country

The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority proudly acknowledges and pays respect to Victoria’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and their rich and enduring cultures.

We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as Australia’s first peoples and as the Traditional Owners and custodians of the lands and waters on which we rely. We pay respect to Elders past and present of the lands where we conduct our work and recognise their ongoing contributions as the first educators on the land now known as Victoria.

Watch now: To find out more about the Arts Foundation to Level 6, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, The Arts Foundation to Level 6’ on the About the Arts page. To find out more about Music Levels 7–10, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, Music Levels 7–10’ on the Resources page.

Rationale and Aims

Rationale

In music, sounds are combined and shaped into a meaningful form. Music has the capacity to motivate, inspire and enrich the lives of all students. Students participate in music learning individually and collectively as listeners, composers and performers. Music learning is embodied learning. It has a significant and unique impact on the creative, sensorimotor, cognitive, emotional, sociocultural and personal competencies of students.

Music exists distinctively in every historical and contemporary culture, and is a basic, shared expression and communication of human experience. Sharing music and ideas about music across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts builds knowledge and enhances empathy, and fosters understanding of other cultures, times, places and contexts. Engagement with music from diverse settings develops an understanding that the same music can be deeply moving for many people and yet have different meaning for each.

Music is a significant element in the diversity and continuity of local and global cultures, particularly the cultures of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Through music, they express connection to Country and Place, challenge the impact of other cultures on their ways of knowing, being, doing and becoming, contribute to the global music community and advocate for change.

Students’ active participation in music, through continuous and developmentally sequential music learning, encourages skills and aesthetic knowledge of increasing depth and complexity over time. Through performing, composing and listening with intent to music, students have access to knowledge, skills and understanding that can be gained in no other way. Music learning enhances students’ capacity to perceive and understand musical concepts, and to recognise music’s contribution in shaping their identity and their ability to explore personal, local and global issues and ideas. Learning in the Music curriculum is aurally based and can be understood without any recourse to notation; learning to read and write music in traditional and graphic forms enables students to access a wide range of music as independent learners. Through the study of Music, students increasingly value the power of music in its ability to transform the heart, soul, mind and spirit of individuals and communities.

Aims

The Music curriculum aims to develop students’:

  • confidence to be creative, innovative, thoughtful, skilful and informed musicians
  • skills to listen, improvise, compose, interpret, perform and respond with intent and purpose
  • aesthetic knowledge and respect for music and music practices across global communities, cultures and musical traditions
  • understanding of music as an aural art form, its relationship with other art forms and contributions to cultures and societies.

Structure

The Music curriculum is presented as one curriculum level at Foundation and then in 2-level bands from Levels 1 to 10.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts bring together learning from Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and Visual Arts. Foundation Levels A to D curriculum levels are developed for students with intellectual disability and learning delay.   

Music comprises 4 interrelated strands:

  • Exploring
  • Developing Practices
  • Creating
  • Presenting.

Exploring

In this strand, students learn as listeners, composers and performers. They explore:

  • diverse examples of how, where and why people create, make, perform, present and respond to music
  • the contexts and roles of music in the lives of individuals and groups across cultures, times, places and communities
  • the diversity and significance of music for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, cultures and communities
  • how music communicates cultural and aesthetic knowledge, purpose, meaning and emotion
  • how music develops empathy and understanding of multiple perspectives.

Students respond using music practices and forms, imagery, sounds, movement, language and digital tools. They listen with intent and use listening skills and imagination to develop ideas in response to stimuli such as music they have listened to, observations, feelings, experiences and research. They explore ways of using and manipulating the elements of music and compositional devices.

Developing Practices

In this strand, students develop practices and skills for listening to, composing, performing and responding to music. They develop knowledge and understanding through play, imagination, experimentation, creative and critical thinking, and practice. They use their voices, instruments, safe practice principles and guidelines, materials such as scores and sheet music, amplification equipment and digital tools as appropriate to develop creative and critical practices including:

  • creative skills and confidence for interpreting, performing and composing music, using the elements of music, listening and aural skills, vocal and instrumental techniques, and available materials and digital tools
  • critical skills for listening to, observing, reflecting on, analysing and evaluating their own and others’ music practices, using language/terminology and embodied practices.

Creating

In this strand, students as artists apply music-specific or multi-arts creative processes to compose music and interpret music for performance. As audiences, they reflect on their work as it develops, for example through observation, using aural skills, analysis, reflection and evaluation.

Individually and collaboratively, using available voices, instruments (acoustic, electric, digital and environmental) and digital tools, students manipulate and exploit elements of music to:

  • compose in forms and styles of interest and relevance through songwriting, improvisation, genre-specific forms such as chamber music, music production, arranging/re-imagining, music for specific purposes or occasions, or music for multi-arts works
  • interpret music composed and performed by others
  • use manual and digital tools to notate, document and record their compositions and interpretations.

Presenting

In this strand, students perform their compositions and interpretations of music composed by other people in informal and formal settings in available physical or virtual spaces. Some performances will be refined; others will be presentations or demonstrations of work in progress. Students:

  • plan, select, design and rehearse their presentations and performances
  • use technical skills and manipulate expressive elements of music to engage audiences and communicate intentions.

Achievement standards

Achievement standards describe what students are typically able to understand and do, and they are the basis for reporting student achievement.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts provide a developmental continuum with the first achievement standard at Foundation Level A, and then at Foundation Level B, Foundation Level C and Foundation Level D.

From Foundation in Music, students progress along a learning continuum that provides the first achievement standard at Foundation, and then at Levels 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.

Content descriptions

In Music, content descriptions sequence and describe the knowledge, understanding and skills that teachers need to teach and students are expected to learn.

Elaborations

Elaborations are examples that provide guidance on how the curriculum may be transformed into a classroom activity or learning opportunity. They are provided as advisory material only.

Learning in Music

Elements of music

The elements of music underpin all Music learning. These are duration/time (including tempo, rhythm and metre), pitch, tone colour/timbre, texture, structure/form, dynamics and articulation.

Musical ideas are conceived, organised and shaped by aspects and combinations of the elements of music. Other elements of music may be included, particularly at Levels 9 and 10, for example elements to align with senior secondary courses.

Listening

Throughout their Music learning, students listen to, experience, analyse, evaluate, perform and compose music from diverse cultures, styles, traditions and contexts. They learn to recognise their subjective preferences and appreciate other people’s diverse perspectives of music.

Students’ approaches to composing and interpreting music as performers are informed by their responses to music that they experience. As they develop their music knowledge and skills, students develop their own musical voice as composers and their own style as performers.

Purposeful or intentional listening skills engage the listener’s mind, senses and emotions. They are used when listening for enjoyment, analysing, responding to, reflecting on, evaluating, composing and performing music. Aural skills are listening skills used to identify and analyse specific elements of music, such as the duration of a note, the interval (distance) between 2 notes or the structure/quality of a chord. Aural skills complement purposeful or active listening and can be used when listening, composing and performing.

Composing

Composing describes the practices and processes used to create music works. It can include, for example, songwriting, improvising, arranging/re-imagining/re-inventing, music production and/or generating. Composing involves creative processes such as developing ideas or intentions, identifying purpose, evaluating and analysing ideas from other music, manipulating elements of music to organise and shape musical ideas, and using compositional devices to structure or extend the music.

Notating, documenting and recording

Notating, documenting and recording involves using available and relevant methods and tools to preserve music for future use. Forms and methods of notating, documenting and recording include staff notation, graphic notation, scores, charts, lead-sheets, and audio and audiovisual recordings. These forms and methods are often associated with genres or styles. Notating, documenting and recording can involve using symbols, images and digital tools.

Performing

Students perform for audiences of one or more in informal settings such as in classes or instrumental lessons, to peers or teachers. They may also present formal performances in a school or public setting. Formats for performances include live (indoor or outdoor), streamed and recorded.

Instruments

Students use available instruments for performing and composing. Instruments can include voice or body, acoustic or electric string, wind, percussion, keyboard instruments, digital instruments and environmental sounds.

Viewpoints

In Music, students respond to musical experiences and ideas through the practices of listening, composing and performing. Throughout their Music learning, students use questions based on viewpoints (personal and imaginative, cultures and worlds, conventions and structure) as an inquiry tool for considering their responses and music practice from multiple perspectives, as artists or as audiences. Students can use questions based on viewpoints to:

  • structure their reasoning and reflecting
  • explore ideas and make decisions
  • explore and develop empathy for multiple perspectives
  • express and celebrate identities, ideas and meaning
  • think deeply about their own music practices and works and music composed and performed by others that they experience.

As they create and respond to music works and experiences, students develop questions to explore ideas, perspectives and meaning. They think and make decisions as artists and as audiences. Questions based on viewpoints encourage students to consider a range of perspectives and to think deeply about their own music works and music created by others.

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level A, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level A, students explore and develop practices through the Arts disciplines by participating in and interacting with arts experiences, elements, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploration together with structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level A, students experience and attend to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works and contribute to the sharing of arts works with others.

Dance

Students interact with the elements of dance to develop an understanding of movement.

Drama

Students interact with the elements of drama and expressive skills.

Media Arts

Students interact with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students interact with the elements of music and instruments.

Visual Arts

Students interact with art elements and materials.

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E14 – The Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing music for different purposes, for example by using music as a cue for transition, relaxation or movement or to reflect different settings and feelings

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAC01 - The Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and responding to concepts through their preferred learning modalities such as visual, kinaesthetic, auditory or tactile

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensorimotor experiences, using gentle movements and interactive play to explore different textures and rhythms

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising movements with support to begin to develop technical skills of body control, posture, strength, balance and coordination

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to rhythmic cues or showing an awareness of a movement they have made

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to choose an object to be included in a dance such as a piece of fabric or a prop

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing tactile and sensory stimuli to evoke a sense of place in a drama work, for example by smelling or feeling seaweed, pampas grass or sand or listening to recorded sounds of the sea during a drama work about a seaside location

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of props, costumes and sounds to contribute to a performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding when things that interest them are being used in a dramatic performance, for example smiling when their favourite music is played as part of a performance or reaching out to a favourite prop being used

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity such as exploring sounds, images and text to contribute to a shared media arts work such as an animation or class presentation in response to an event or experience, for example being part of a presentation to their school on a class activity or a response to a story

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving shapes or icons on a screen to create a media presentation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an artwork after experimenting with images and texts in response to a story about an animal or imaginary creature

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the creation of a presentation in response to a film they have viewed with the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to the variety of sounds that can be created with voice and body percussion, for example by listening to, watching or feeling the vibrations of sound effects

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and attending to the use of sound effects to accompany stories, rhymes, games and pictures, for example participating in choosing and attending to the kinds of sounds that complement these activities

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an object, equipment or instrument to contribute to a group song, for example by activating a switch to play a sound, striking a drum or pressing keys on a musical keyboard

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing an interest in experimenting with making sounds using voice and body percussion, for example by imitating interesting sounds made by another, repeating interesting sounds they discover or showing some creativity in using their voice and body to make sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity, exploring materials to contribute to a shared visual artwork in response to an event or experience, for example returning from a community walk and exploring colours, shapes, textures and objects that could contribute to a group artwork and then expressing ideas about what was experienced on the walk (such as crunching leaves, texture of bark and colours)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving objects or images to create an artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity to repurpose materials into a shared artwork based on experimentation, for example using cardboard or objects that create sound and expressing ideas about an imaginary animal or object

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a visit to an exhibition or art gallery and expressing ideas about the artworks using different materials, sounds or gestures

elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E02 – The Arts

elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing a recording of their movement or contribution to a dance work (individual and group efforts), for example listening to an audio recording or viewing a video or photograph of their performance

elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing their engagement in a drama work with others in the classroom, for example by interacting with props and puppets or by responding to their teacher in-role

elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a role alongside others, supported by staff in the role, for example by participating in a class or school performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the presentation of their drama work in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of a media arts work that they have contributed to, such as in a digital display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or on the school website)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing images that represent an experience or ‘tell a story’

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a reaction to an event or experience by using sounds and images

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a class presentation of an event or experience around a topic, for example by using sounds, gestures or movement in response to a learning experience, class outing or excursion

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness that others listen to and respond to their voice or sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: having their sound contribution recorded and played back to them and the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of being involved in performing for others, for example by responding to the clapping of others

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of their visual artwork, such as in a display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or sent home to families)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to express ideas about work they have created with another person

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to their artworks being shown in a digital presentation, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements when an image of their artwork is displayed on a screen

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a review of a presentation of class artworks and indicating their feelings about the artworks, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements to indicate their preferences for artwork features such as subject, elements and emotions

elaborations.elaboration_text: being supported to engage in aspects of dramatic role-play or process drama of a recent experience or event, for example during the re-enactment of a bus journey with the teacher in the role of the bus driver, students sitting behind in rows, the sounds of the bus and being rocked gently in a chair

elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the collective experience of a dramatic performance as an audience member, for example when experiencing a dramatised familiar short story or puppet show at school or during an excursion

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring characters and settings through images, sounds and multimodal texts, for example by listening to a soundscape of the ocean while experiencing textural elements of water and sand

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring media arts works created by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people

elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in the use of technologies to capture images or sounds, for example by using a switch or button to activate media equipment to capture an image or to record a sound

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to composition by attending to images and/or sounds when given a choice or having their vocalisations recorded and compiled into a co-created artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering ways of using body percussion to explore rhythm and sound, for example by clapping or tapping

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in sounds or the representation of sounds in their environment, for example by attending to a musical sound or vibration by turning their head or body as the sound or sensation travels or by associating music with routines such as musical cues for the start and finish of activities or the school bell

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in multisensory opportunities to explore music practices such as by listening or feeling, experimenting or playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to associate sounds or vibrations with their source, for example by touching a drum in response to a sensation

elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of art equipment, for example by holding various objects, mark-making tools and materials for short periods of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a visual artwork to explore ideas, for example by reaching towards, touching or exploring objects, environments, colour, texture or materials

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and interacting with two- or three-dimensional artworks that have been created using digital technologies and tools, such as images, soundscapes, interactive artworks, public art or screen-based works

elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the sensory elements of dance such as the movement of a dancer, a prop used, clothing worn or music played

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to moments of interest and focusing on a shared point of interest, for example by showing fleeting interest in a brightly coloured and textured cloak worn by others in role-play or attending or responding to changes in performance such as lighting changes or the commencement of music

elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and responding to opportunities to explore the sensory experiences of drama, including sights, sounds, smells and textures of drama, for example choosing preferred items from a selection of sensory materials such as fabrics, objects, crunchy paper, a shaker or water in a bottle

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: being supported to engage in aspects of dramatic role-play or process drama of a recent experience or event, for example during the re-enactment of a bus journey with the teacher in the role of the bus driver, students sitting behind in rows, the sounds of the bus and being rocked gently in a chair

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to the collective experience of a dramatic performance as an audience member, for example when experiencing a dramatised familiar short story or puppet show at school or during an excursion

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring characters and settings through images, sounds and multimodal texts, for example by listening to a soundscape of the ocean while experiencing textural elements of water and sand

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring media arts works created by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.

elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in the use of technologies to capture images or sounds, for example by using a switch or button to activate media equipment to capture an image or to record a sound

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to composition by attending to images and/or sounds when given a choice or having their vocalisations recorded and compiled into a co-created artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering ways of using body percussion to explore rhythm and sound, for example by clapping or tapping

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in sounds or the representation of sounds in their environment, for example by attending to a musical sound or vibration by turning their head or body as the sound or sensation travels or by associating music with routines such as musical cues for the start and finish of activities or the school bell

elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in multisensory opportunities to explore music practices such as by listening or feeling, experimenting or playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to associate sounds or vibrations with their source, for example by touching a drum in response to a sensation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of art equipment, for example by holding various objects, mark-making tools and materials for short periods of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a visual artwork to explore ideas, for example by reaching towards, touching or exploring objects, environments, colour, texture or materials

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and interacting with two- or three-dimensional artworks that have been created using digital technologies and tools, such as images, soundscapes, interactive artworks, public art or screen-based works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring artworks made by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to develop an awareness of the culture and practices of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and responding to concepts through their preferred learning modalities such as visual, kinaesthetic, auditory or tactile

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensorimotor experiences, using gentle movements and interactive play to explore different textures and rhythms

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising movements with support to begin to develop technical skills of body control, posture, strength, balance and coordination

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to rhythmic cues or showing an awareness of a movement they have made

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to choose an object to be included in a dance such as a piece of fabric or a prop

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing tactile and sensory stimuli to evoke a sense of place in a drama work, for example by smelling or feeling seaweed, pampas grass or sand or listening to recorded sounds of the sea during a drama work about a seaside location

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of props, costumes and sounds to contribute to a performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding when things that interest them are being used in a dramatic performance, for example smiling when their favourite music is played as part of a performance or reaching out to a favourite prop being used

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E12 – The Arts

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Music - Foundation Level B (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level B, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level B, students explore, develop practices and contribute to creating through the Arts disciplines by participating and engaging in arts experiences, elements, forms, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploring ideas in arts works from different people and communities, within structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

Students contribute to the co-creation of group arts works in response to a shared experience or observation.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level B, students engage with arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works that explore ideas and they identify their contribution to the presentation of arts works to others.

Dance

Students engage with the elements of dance to develop personal movement.

Drama

Students engage with the elements of drama and expressive skills to develop characters, situations and/or settings.

Media Arts

Students engage with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students engage with the elements of music and instruments to develop sounds.

Visual Arts

Students engage with art elements and materials.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Music - Foundation Level C (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level C, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level C, students explore ideas communicated through the arts works of different people and communities.

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas through the use of art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students create and share their arts works in informal settings such as the classroom.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level C, students respond to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create arts works and present these to others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works.

They use their bodies, objects and/or materials when responding to personal experiences to create dance works.

Drama

Students explore stories and the elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to develop drama works.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas when responding to personal experiences to create drama works.

Media Arts

Students explore media arts forms, language and technologies to construct media arts works.

They use media languages, processes and technologies when responding to personal experiences to create media arts works.

Music

Students explore sound sources, instruments and elements of music to develop music works.

They use elements of music and instruments when responding to personal experiences to create music works.

Visual Arts

Students explore art elements, materials and techniques.

They use art elements, materials and techniques when responding to personal experiences to create visual arts works.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Music - Foundation Level D (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level D, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level D, students explore how ideas are represented in a variety of ways by different people and communities.

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas by experimenting with different art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students share meaning through their creation of arts works and share their arts works with familiar people.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level D, students respond to stories, observations and ideas about arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create, share and present arts works with others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works that represent ideas.

They use movement and elements of dance to communicate ideas in dance works.

Drama

Students explore the elements of drama, expressive skills and production elements to develop drama works that represent ideas.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to represent characters and settings to communicate ideas in drama works.

Media Arts

Students use media languages, processes and technologies to construct media arts works and to represent ideas and stories.

They develop and present media arts works that represent ideas and stories to audiences.

Music

Students explore sound sources, elements of music and instruments to develop music works that represent ideas.

They use elements of music and instruments to communicate ideas and meaning in music works.

Visual Arts

Students respond to ideas in visual arts works and explore art elements, materials, techniques and processes to develop arts works that express ideas in different arts forms.

They use art elements, materials, techniques and processes to communicate their ideas in arts works in different arts forms.

content_descriptions.text: explore how ideas are represented in arts works by different people and communities

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to stories, ideas and actions through dance, for example by moving in response to music, shared stories or visual media

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with the elements of dance such as body, space, time and energy through various movement exercises

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing fundamental movements safely while copying dance ideas, for example by falling like an autumn leaf, floating like a cloud or gliding like a bird

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using expressive skills to communicate a character’s feelings at different points in a familiar story

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking part in purposeful dramatic play, focusing on experiencing different roles and situations

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using characters such as puppets or figurines to act out elements of stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring media arts works produced by different media sources such as streaming services, social media and broadcast media

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ use of media arts forms to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Culture, Country and Place

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss and express an opinion about the way an artwork has been created, including expressing features they like best in others’ artworks

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss features of their own and others’ artworks, for example by identifying the main materials used, characteristics of the artwork or what the piece is about

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying rhythms and music patterns and adapting to changes to rhythm and tempo

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating musical patterns, for example by clapping, singing or playing an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar instrument timbres, for example when identifying the sound of a drum or triangle

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing different types of music from various communities, cultures and genres

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using art elements in their artwork after exploring different art, craft and design styles and techniques from different cultures (such as African, Oceanian and Asian cultures) and artistic periods, for example by incorporating expressionism or fauvism

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ use of art elements and visual language to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Culture, Country and Place

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing guided discussions to explore, identify and express the features of their own and others’ artworks, for example by identifying the main materials used, aspects and details of the work they are drawn to or characteristics of their artworks

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing art in their lives and communities, for example contributing to the creation of a class diary of art experiences by exploring artworks and their purpose or matching artworks to their location

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and practising a range of movement types, for example by using light and heavy, fast and slow movements

elaborations.elaboration_text: practising a range of fundamental movements to music, for example by walking, running, marching, galloping, skipping, crawling (locomotor), bending, stretching, twisting or turning (non-locomotor)

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to communicate a character’s feelings at specific points in a familiar story

elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in drama activities using expressive skills and some elements of drama to communicate a character’s feelings or narrative ideas

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring possibilities for roles and situations when participating in group drama and role-play

elaborations.elaboration_text: learning how to work safely during drama activities and following the safety rules of the space

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning how to use a variety of media technologies and using elements such as drawing, sound mixing, editing and addition of special effects

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with a digital device to capture still images, for example by zooming the lens in and out or reviewing captured images

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: following visual procedural steps to create a photo story using software

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: imagining how the characters in a story might dress or move and making still or moving images to communicate ideas about the characters

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising music, for example by using classroom instruments, body percussion or accessible technologies

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing, using body percussion and/or playing instruments to explore expressive possibilities, improvise patterns and to practise chants, songs and rhymes

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to describe the sounds of instruments, for example communicating that the sounds are scratchy, soft or loud

elaborations.name: VC2AFDD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning a song used by groups in the community, such as traditional Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ songs, and following cultural protocols when creating or presenting them

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. elaborations.elaboration_text: distinguishing and describing changes in music and comparing pieces of music, for example communicating ‘This music started fast and then became slow.’, ‘This music had lots of instruments, but this music only had voices.’ or ‘This music was spiky, but this music was smooth.’

elaborations.elaboration_text: mixing colours to make and explore secondary colours

elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the qualities and properties of materials such as paint, crayons, clay and found objects

elaborations.elaboration_text: dramatising rhymes, stories, legends and traditional stories from various cultures, including their own, for example by using actions, pictures, words or puppets to tell a story

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a media arts work for a social purpose such as a school community event

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring arts viewpoints and considering societies and cultures, for example considering the images they could use to tell their story or represent an event

elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the features of their own and others’ music, identifying the main elements and the features they like

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying musical patterns and changes to rhythm and tempo in music they have created

elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to classroom discussion about aspects of music they have made or experienced

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying where they might experience music in their lives and communities, such as at celebrations or cultural events

elaborations.elaboration_text: describing music using their preferred communication modality and learnt music terminology, for example saying ‘loud’, ‘soft’, ‘happy’ or ‘sad’

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.

elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using and repeating known movement sequences in their own improvisations

elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting movement with the mood and speed of the music to create a sequence of movements

elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss features of dance, such as what a dance is about or its costumes or movements

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying where they have experienced dance in their lives, such as at community or social events, exploring what these dances are about and using their observations to create dance, for example by contributing different movements to parts of a group dance

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.elaboration_text: using their imagination to create drama and dance, for example by contributing different voices or sounds for parts of a story or chant

elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to participate in class discussions about likes, dislikes and opinions about a play

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the features of their own and others’ performances, for example by discussing the features they liked best, characters and production areas

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of media equipment, for example when creating a poster or by using graphics software to create visual and sound picture cards or when creating and presenting their own rhythmic composition or sound piece

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a media arts work for a social purpose such as a school community event

elaborations.elaboration_text: using a variety of art elements to create a series of images that portrays them as a superhero or villain

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring arts viewpoints and considering societies and cultures, for example considering the images they could use to tell their story or represent an event

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the features of their own and others’ music, identifying the main elements and the features they like

elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to classroom discussion about aspects of music they have made or experienced

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying where they might experience music in their lives and communities, such as at celebrations or cultural events

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to discussion on the social and cultural elements of music, for example responding to or posing questions such as ‘Where is this music from?’, ‘Why was it made?’ or ‘What is it about?’

elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and talking about music and instruments in different contexts and from different cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFDC01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the purpose of music and its role as a social and emotional outlet

elaborations.elaboration_text: using their understanding of art elements and processes to create different meanings in artworks

elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how they can use different visual conventions to create artworks

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing a familiar dance that communicates ideas, observations or experiences with others

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to describe some of the characteristics of their dance and expressing the features they like best in their dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using expressive skills and production elements to engage the audience, for example by facing the audience or using props

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing and presenting their dance in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing in a simple drama work or play

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing aspects of known stories by presenting drama alongside others

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring or re-enacting a cultural or community story with the assistance of representatives of the community

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing and performing sequences of ideas to communicate stories through drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating their understanding of something (such as a poem, a story or a piece of music) through drama and dance, for example moving like the animals in a poem, finding different ways to move to music or a teacher prompt, moving as if they were outside on a windy day after hearing a story about the wind or ‘freezing’ like a statue

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: displaying and discussing their media arts works with others

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a visual and/or audio story or a poster using graphics software with the intention to meet an audience need, for example by retelling a familiar story using a combination of images, symbols or sounds or a poster that recounts an event to share with the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing class experiences and presenting them in the form of a class photo story or using PowerPoint

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: assisting in the production and presentation of an artwork for a particular purpose, for example helping to create a poster about expectations when using cameras in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing music in a way that shows emerging music knowledge and skills, for example by performing music at a celebration that demonstrates elements of music such as rhythm

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating music to communicate ideas, concepts, observations, feelings and/or experiences, for example by choosing and combining sounds to create compositions for presentation

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: employing patterns of body movement such as clapping or stamping and performing accompaniments to familiar music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting using music technologies such as digital audio workstation software

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating appropriate audience behaviour when in the classroom and when attending school functions, for example by watching for an extended period of time and responding to performance, clapping at the conclusion and identifying strategies that will help them with this (such as cues and images)

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss features of their own and others’ visual arts works using a few short spoken or written sentences, for example expressing the features they like best in their own artwork, identifying the main materials used in artworks or describing some of the characteristics of their artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss ideas such as themes in relation to the display of artworks, such as at the local gallery or in their classroom

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E26 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: deciding which of their artworks to display and how to display them

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E27 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and identifying the roles of artist and audience

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2AFDE01 - The Arts

elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to stories, ideas and actions through dance, for example by moving in response to music, shared stories or visual media

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with the elements of dance such as body, space, time and energy through various movement exercises

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing fundamental movements safely while copying dance ideas, for example by falling like an autumn leaf, floating like a cloud or gliding like a bird

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using expressive skills to communicate a character’s feelings at different points in a familiar story

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: taking part in purposeful dramatic play, focusing on experiencing different roles and situations

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using characters such as puppets or figurines to act out elements of stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring media arts works produced by different media sources such as streaming services, social media and broadcast media

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ use of media arts forms to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Culture, Country and Place

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss and express an opinion about the way an artwork has been created, including expressing features they like best in others’ artworks

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss features of their own and others’ artworks, for example by identifying the main materials used, characteristics of the artwork or what the piece is about

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying rhythms and music patterns and adapting to changes to rhythm and tempo

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating musical patterns, for example by clapping, singing or playing an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar instrument timbres, for example when identifying the sound of a drum or triangle

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing different types of music from various communities, cultures and genres

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using art elements in their artwork after exploring different art, craft and design styles and techniques from different cultures (such as African, Oceanian and Asian cultures) and artistic periods, for example by incorporating expressionism or fauvism

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ use of art elements and visual language to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Culture, Country and Place

elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing guided discussions to explore, identify and express the features of their own and others’ artworks, for example by identifying the main materials used, aspects and details of the work they are drawn to or characteristics of their artworks

elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing art in their lives and communities, for example contributing to the creation of a class diary of art experiences by exploring artworks and their purpose or matching artworks to their location

elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.elaboration_text: practising music, for example by using classroom instruments, body percussion or accessible technologies

elaborations.elaboration_text: singing, using body percussion and/or playing instruments to explore expressive possibilities, improvise patterns and to practise chants, songs and rhymes

curriculum_level_description.body:
Learning in Music builds on the Victorian Early Years Learning and Development Framework (VEYLDF) and each student’s prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for play-based approaches that integrate arts learning experiences across the Arts disciplines and/or specialist teaching. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline and examples that span across the disciplines.

In Foundation, students explore music by learning to listen and respond to music, becoming aware of the elements of beat, rhythm, pitch, dynamics and tempo as they sing, play, improvise and move to music. They learn to feel the beat, sing with pitch awareness and discriminate between sound and silence, loud and soft, and fast and slow. Working individually and collaboratively with peers and teachers, students draw on their imaginations, stimulus materials such as images, short stories, poems, and real-life experiences. They share their work with peers in informal settings such as the classroom.

Students talk about music that they hear in the community, identifying what they enjoy and why, and learn that the arts are central to all cultures. They reflect on their music experiences verbally and in embodied ways.

In Foundation, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to music they encounter at home, at school and in the community through listening and performing; for example, singing songs and moving to music
  • developing creative and critical practices and skills by experimenting with instruments and voices to discover different ways of producing sound to accompany songs and singing games
  • using music elements such as beat, rhythm, tempo, pitch and dynamics to create specific effects when making music with voice, body or instrument
  • sharing music they have learnt and/or composed in informal settings.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Foundation, students describe the music they listen to at school, at home and in the community, identifying what they enjoy and why. Students sing with pitch awareness and respond to the beat and simple rhythm patterns. They explore contrasting sounds and improvise with them, using imagination and skills to create music. They sing and play instruments to communicate their experiences and ideas.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 1 and 2, students listen to and experiment with a range of sounds. They develop skills in imagining, creating and performing music that explores their ideas about the world. They work individually and in collaboration with peers and teachers, drawing on their imagination, works of fiction, real-life experiences and learnings from across the curriculum to support their engagement in Arts learning as artists and as audiences.

Students explore music that they experience at home or school or through family and community events. They connect with composers and/or performers who live and work in the local community and beyond, for example by experiencing live or virtual performances.

In Levels 1 and 2, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to:
    • music across cultures, communities and other contexts through listening and performing; for example, singing songs or moving to music
    • examples of music composed and/or performed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
  • developing creative and critical practices and skills:
    • in creative practices for composing and performing, such as skills for listening, singing and playing instruments, and, as appropriate, using notation such as graphic notation
    • in critical practices for observing, reflecting on and responding to music they experience (including music they compose and/or perform)
  • composing, singing and playing instruments using the elements of music, such as duration/time (beat, rhythm and tempo), pitch, dynamics and expression, texture and/or timbre
  • performing and sharing music they have learnt and/or composed in informal settings such as classroom presentations.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 2, students identify where they experience music. They describe where, why and how people across cultures, communities and other contexts experience music. Students demonstrate listening skills when hearing and when making music. They use the elements of music to improvise and/or compose music. They share their music-making with audiences in informal settings.

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, students continue to explore music they hear at home, school or through family and community. They connect with composers and performers through live or virtual performances, and take inspiration from the world around them to create music individually and collaboratively with peers and teachers.

In Levels 3 and 4, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to music from different cultures, times and places:
    • through listening to and singing songs such as those used in children's games or for storytelling
    • by learning about how music is used in popular culture and media
    • by learning about music composed and/or performed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples that communicates their connection to and responsibility for Country and Place
  • developing creative and critical skills for music-making:
    • by learning skills for listening, singing and playing instruments, using a variety of notation such as graphic notation
    • through reflecting on and responding to music they experience, including music they compose and perform
  • composing, creating and making music using different instruments, their voice and body, and the elements of music such as beat and rhythm, tempo, pitch, dynamics and expression, texture and timbre
  • presenting or performing music they have learnt and/or composed in informal settings, such as their classroom, or sharing in safe online classrooms.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 4, students identify and describe how elements of music are used in music they compose and/or perform. They recall where, when, why and how music is created and presented across cultures, times, places and other contexts, including the music of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. Students use listening skills when performing, composing and listening to music. Students use music knowledge and skills to create music in a range of forms that communicates ideas, perspectives and meaning. They perform their work in formal and informal settings.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. content_descriptions.name: VC2AMU4D01 - Music
content_descriptions.text: develop listening skills and skills for working with elements of music when singing and playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4D01-E01 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing the skill of singing in tune by listening to a note and matching it with their voice through activities such as singing games or call-and-response songs

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4D01-E02 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the elements of music with the use of their voice and how it can be used in different ways such as speaking, singing, rapping or chanting softly or loudly and using warm-up activities and games to practise this skill

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4D01-E03 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with different dynamics (volumes), tempi (speeds) and articulation when singing and playing instruments to create different moods in music

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4D01-E04 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and exploring the use of the elements of music in different pieces of music, such as identifying the melody, rhythm, accompaniment and tone colours, and how they contribute to the overall effect of the music

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4D01-E05 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising reading staff, graphic and invented notation while rehearsing and performing, and exploring options for visually representing sounds

content_descriptions.name: VC2AMU4C01 - Music
content_descriptions.text: work with elements of music to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning when composing and practising for performance

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4C01-E01 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing lyrics or melodies for songs, raps or chants to communicate an idea, and using formats such as graphic or staff notation, a lead-sheet or an audio recording to notate, document or record their work

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4C01-E02 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: using available technologies to create accompaniments; for example, improvising patterns (body percussion, classroom instruments) and recording as a loop or using digital tools to notate or document music appropriate to the style

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4C01-E03 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: improvising phrases of music on an instrument to practise known notes and rhythmic patterns or to extend the range of notes they can play on an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4C01-E04 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: manipulating the elements of music, such as dynamics and tempi, to express different characters or dramatic action and emotions when composing music for a screen-based work or to accompany drama, such as a retelling of a familiar children’s story

content_descriptions.name: VC2AMU4P01 - Music
content_descriptions.text: sing and play music they have learnt and/or created to audiences in formal and informal settings

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4P01-E01 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing music such as unison songs, rounds and instrumental music arranged for small ensembles that feature melody and accompaniment parts, such as ostinato or drones

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4P01-E02 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: introducing performances by sharing information such as the intended purposes of their compositions with others, and documenting how they used the elements of music when composing and/or performing

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4P01-E03 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning and rehearsing their music for a live or virtual performance; for example, deciding where the performers will stand and how they will begin and end, practising following cues from the music and other members of the group, and planning how to introduce their performances to audiences using spoken, written or audiovisual formats

elaborations.name: VC2AMU4P01-E04 - Music
elaborations.elaboration_text: refining their compositions and performances based on peer and teacher suggestions and with a focus on specific music techniques such as ways to hold beaters to elicit the required sound from a percussion instrument and exploiting specific elements of music

as_extracts.name: AMUS4-E04
as_extracts.description: Students use music knowledge and skills to create music in a range of forms that communicates ideas, perspectives and meaning.
